metadata.title: A new Proof of the Corona Problem

nodes.name: Hardy space $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$
nodes.statement: The commutative Banach algebra $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ consists of bounded holomorphic functions on the unit disc $\mathbb{D}$ with the supremum norm.
nodes.statement_clean: Banach algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on the unit disc.

nodes.name: Spectrum (maximal ideal space) $\mathbb{S}$
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{S}$ is the space of closed maximal ideals of $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$; it contains $\mathbb{D}$ as an open subspace via $z \mapsto \{f : f(z)=0\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximal ideal space of $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$, containing the disc as open subspace.

nodes.name: Corona
nodes.statement: The corona is the complement of the closure of $\mathbb{D}$ in the spectrum $\mathbb{S}$ (terminology due to Newman 1959).

nodes.name: Carleson measure
nodes.statement: A measure introduced by Carleson, used to control the length of curves in the disc that wind around the zeros of a bounded analytic function.
nodes.statement_clean: Measure-theoretic tool for controlling boundary behavior of $H^\infty$ functions.

nodes.name: Bezout's Formulation of the Corona Problem
nodes.statement: Given $f_1,\ldots,f_N \in H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ with $|f_1|+\cdots+|f_N|>\delta>0$ on $\mathbb{D}$, do there exist $g_1,\ldots,g_N \in H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ with $f_1g_1+\cdots+f_Ng_N=1$ on $\mathbb{D}$?
nodes.statement_clean: Find bounded analytic $g_k$ solving the Bezout identity given lower bound on $\sum|f_k|$.

nodes.name: Corona lower bound condition
nodes.statement: $|f_1|+|f_2|+\cdots+|f_N| > \delta > 0$ on $\mathbb{D}$.

nodes.name: Bezout identity
nodes.statement: $f_1g_1 + f_2g_2 + \cdots + f_Ng_N = 1$ on $\mathbb{D}$.

nodes.name: Trivial nonanalytic Bezout solution
nodes.statement: $g_k = \dfrac{\bar{f}_k}{\sum_{j=1}^N |f_j|^2}$ solves the Bezout equation but is not analytic.

nodes.name: Rudin's subset-sum lemma
nodes.statement: If $z_1,\ldots,z_N$ are complex numbers, there exists a subset $S \subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $\left|\sum_{k\in S} z_k\right| \geq \frac{1}{\pi}\sum_{k=1}^N |z_k|$.
nodes.origin_citation: Walter Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis (3rd ed.)

nodes.name: Pointwise Rudin lemma for complex functions
nodes.statement: If $f_1(z),\ldots,f_N(z)$ are complex functions on a domain $\Omega$, then for every $z\in\Omega$ there exists a nonempty subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $\left|\sum_{k\in S} f_k(z)\right| \geq \frac{1}{\pi}\sum_{k=1}^N |f_k(z)|$.
assumptions: $f_1,\ldots,f_N : \Omega \to \mathbb{C}$ are complex functions on a domain $\Omega$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: By contradiction: suppose no such $S$ exists for some $z_0 \in \Omega$; then $f_1(z_0),\ldots,f_N(z_0)$ violate Lemma 3.1, contradicting Rudin's lemma.

nodes.name: Subset nonvanishing theorem
nodes.statement: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_N \in H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ with $|f_1|+\cdots+|f_N|>\delta>0$ on $\mathbb{D}$. Then for each $z\in\mathbb{D}$ there exists a subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that $\sum_{k\in S}f_k(z)\neq 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 3.2 to obtain $S$ with $\left|\sum_{k\in S}f_k(z)\right|\geq \frac{1}{\pi}\sum|f_k(z)|>\delta>0$, hence $\sum_{k\in S} f_k(z)\neq 0$.

nodes.name: Corona Theorem (Bezout form)
nodes.statement: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_N \in H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ satisfy Bezout's formulation of the corona problem. Then there exist $g_1,\ldots,g_N \in H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ such that $f_1g_1+f_2g_2+\cdots+f_Ng_N=1$.

nodes.name: Proof of the Corona Theorem (Theorem 3.4)
nodes.statement: Case split on whether $G(z)=\sum f_k(z)$ vanishes; in either case construct bounded analytic $g_k$ via $1/G(z)$ on the appropriate index subset $S$ given by Theorem 3.3.

nodes.name: Easy case: $G$ zero-free
nodes.statement: If $G(z)=f_1(z)+\cdots+f_N(z)\neq 0$ for every $z\in\mathbb{D}$, set $g_k(z)=1/G(z)$; each $g_k$ is analytic on $\mathbb{D}$ and $\sum f_kg_k=1$.

nodes.name: General case via Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: Otherwise, by Theorem 3.3 there exists a subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ for each $z\in\mathbb{D}$ with $G(z)=\sum_{k\in S}f_k(z)\neq 0$.

nodes.name: Define the $g_k$ on $S$ and outside $S$
nodes.statement: Set $g_k(z)=1/G(z)$ for $k\in S$ and $g_k(z)=0$ for $k\notin S$; each $g_k$ is bounded analytic on $\mathbb{D}$.

nodes.name: Verify Bezout identity
nodes.statement: Compute $\sum_{k=1}^N f_k(z)g_k(z) = \sum_{k\in S} f_k(z)g_k(z) + \sum_{k\notin S} f_k(z)\cdot 0 = \sum_{k\in S} f_k(z)/G(z) = 1$.

nodes.name: Contradiction setup
nodes.statement: Assume that no nonempty $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfies the inequality at every $z\in\Omega$.

nodes.name: Reduce to numerical case
nodes.statement: Then for every nonempty $S$ there is some $z_0\in\Omega$ where the inequality fails; the values $f_1(z_0),\ldots,f_N(z_0)$ are complex numbers violating the bound for every $S$.

nodes.name: Contradict Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: This contradicts Lemma 3.1 (Rudin), which guarantees such an $S$ for any complex tuple. Therefore Lemma 3.2 holds.

nodes.name: Carleson's Corona Theorem
nodes.statement: The open unit disc $\mathbb{D}$ is dense in the maximal ideal space $\mathbb{S}$ of $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$; equivalently, the corona is empty.
assumptions: $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ as the algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{D}$

nodes.name: Extensibility to bounded planar domains and several variables
nodes.statement: The proof on $\mathbb{D}$ extends easily to any bounded domain in $\mathbb{C}$; the author hopes the method extends to domains in several complex variables.

nodes.name: Method bypasses prior corona machinery
nodes.statement: The present proof avoids the methods (Carleson measures, $\bar{\partial}$-equation techniques of Hormander/Wolff) previously developed to construct solutions of the corona problem.

nodes.name: Corona theorem in higher dimensions / general planar domains
nodes.statement: It remains an open question whether versions of the corona theorem hold for every planar domain or for higher-dimensional domains; Cole exhibited an infinitely-connected Riemann surface where the corona theorem fails.
